deduplication_review.round-rule-page139: Forty-four component witnesses resolve to eight forms: four complete handed long rules, one tight quarter-circle corner shared by the 3/6-point impressions, one curved junction shared by both sizes, and separate broad 4-point and fine 2-point corners. deduplication_review.binding-covers: Eight binding corner witnesses resolve to one complete interlaced square meander design and seven rotations. The front lower-left corner is preferred. deduplication_review.brass-circles-and-braces: Twenty native circles retain numbered diameter and line-weight proportions. Twenty-four brace impressions resolve to thirteen forms and eleven rotated repeats; the opposed No.11 specimens have different lengths and curvature proportions. Full native comparisons and rotated retrieval find no exact prior forms. Existing small outlined-circle symbols have much heavier relative strokes. Tables and instructional margin diagrams remain documentary compositions.
deduplication_review.signs-page18: Printed page18has222sign impressions:40distinct additions,19repeats,157existing Boston references and6unresolved identities. Native cross-book comparison records relative construction and printing defects separately. Twelve additional references avoid duplicate artwork; six complete source-supported forms add the narrow italic percent, plain-ended scruple, widely separated equality, broad comparison angle, detached-bar plus-minus and narrow acute angle. Differences in stock length, source resolution and ink spread do not establish a new design. This is a design correspondence, not evidence of shared physical matrices or an inferred Baltimore point size.
entries.quality_selection: Retain the Baltimore drawing: its approximately5–7pixel native strokes and23–24pixel centre separation provide more source detail than the later2–3pixel strokes. The1897upperline is particularly faint; the Census witnesses remain smaller and unevenly inked.

entries.name: Unequal double rule, 4-point
entries.reason: Different line-weight and gap proportions from the existing Baltimore pairs; neither arbitrary stock length nor the printed body size alone defines this design. The four-point pair has a narrower gap relative to its heavier line than the six- and ten-point pairs. The six- and ten-point faces retain different gap-to-stroke proportions. The twelve-point form combines a broad solid band and a much finer lower rule with a wider relative gap than the closest Baltimore heavy/fine examples.
